content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any relevant ageing/performance notes. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates and their humidity-ageing transparency losses; eliminate any candidate with >10% loss after the 10-year-equivalent test."},{"id":"s2","description":"For each remaining compliant candidate, run simulate_separation at representative thicknesses across the allowed 1–6 cm range, e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm. Record the returned separation values numerically with record_results."},{"id":"s3","description":"Identify the best-performing candidate/thickness region from the coarse scan. For the top candidate(s), run additional simulate_separation points at finer thickness increments around the apparent maximum within 1–6 cm, especially near neighboring coarse-scan points. Record all numeric results."},{"id":"s4","description":"Compare all simulated pion/kaon separation results only among candidates satisfying the humidity-loss hard requirement. Select the radiator and thickness with the highest separation at 10 GeV/c; if results are tied or nearly tied, prefer the thinner option to reduce material budget."},{"id":"s5","description":"Prepare the final step result: state the recommended radiator and thickness, the achieved simulated pion/kaon separation, and confirm compliance with the ≤10% transparency-loss requirement and the 1–6 cm thickness constraint."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Radiator-R3","thickness_cm":3.75,"justification":"Select Radiator-R3 at 3.75 cm because it gives the best simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c among all evaluated eligible candidates and thicknesses: 4.869 sigma.
